WITH u AS (SELECT substr(p.ordered_on,1,4) yr, sum(l.amount) amt FROM erp_purchase_orders p JOIN erp_po_lines l USING(po_id)
 LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT po_id FROM erp_receipts) r USING(po_id) WHERE l.pounds>0 AND r.po_id IS NULL GROUP BY 1)
SELECT round(min(amt)) min_unrec_yr, round(max(amt)) max_unrec_yr,
 (SELECT round(sum(amount)/10) FROM erp_credit_memos) credits_per_yr,
 (SELECT round(sum(ql.quantity*ql.unit_price)/10) FROM erp_quotes q JOIN erp_quote_lines ql USING(quote_id) WHERE q.kind='new' AND q.status<>'' AND q.estimator_id IN (113,115,118)) low_hit_est_value_per_yr
FROM u

I've saved `hypotheses.json` with twelve hypotheses. Each has a claim that could turn out false, a dollar size from the queries (q76–q99), what would support or weaken it, and the columns it needs. Revenue runs about $23–33M a year (q76).

| Hypothesis | Size per year | Significance rank | Answerable rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 Repeat-order prices and the invoice uplift lagged the 2021–22 steel rise | ~$2.5–3.1M in 2021–22; ~$0.5–0.6M since | 1 | 4 |
| H2 Paid hours not clocked to any job are growing (24.5% → 34.9% of paid hours) | ~$1.47M unclocked; ~$0.49M of it is growth | 2 | 11 |
| H3 Expired new-part quotes are winnable with follow-up | ~$4.1M of quoted value expires | 3 | 12 |
| H4 Routing estimates are too high outside welding (actual/estimate 0.72–0.87), pricing new quotes out | stake is $1.6M lost plus $4.1M expired quoted value | 4 | 10 |
| H5 Scrap is concentrated in a few parts, work centres or employees | $0.17–0.35M material; ~$0.76M at selling price | 5 | 5 |
| H6 Material POs with no receipt are duplicates still booked as cost | $0.15–0.35M | 6 | 9 |
| H7 Late payment is concentrated in a few customers (28 customers carry 41% of overdue dollar-days) | ~$0.11M carrying cost on ~$1.4M extra receivables | 7 | 2 |
| H8 Estimator hit-rate gaps (0.16–0.30) remain after controlling for customer and year | tens of thousands | 9 | 8 |
| H9 Some customers or part families are unprofitable | probably small | 8 | 6 |
| H10 Late material receipts drive late shipments (2021: 75% late vs 18%) | direct cost ≤ ~$0.1M | 10 | 3 |
| H11 Jobs released on a superseded revision cause wrong-revision scrap and returns | ~$0.06M plus part of $38k credits | 11 | 7 |
| H12 Freight isn't fully billed to customers | ~$0 | 12 | 1 |

The two rankings differ sharply. The biggest-dollar questions (H2, H3, H4) are among the hardest to answer from these records, and the easiest (H12, H7, H10) are small.

**Expected to be "fine":**
- **H12:** freight already looks false. Billed freight equals shipment freight on every invoice, in every year and shipping method (q82).
- **H9:** looks fine at segment level. Every segment earns $159–168 of revenue after material per clocked hour, and no customer is below $60 (q90). Part family and order size are still untested.
- **H8:** may disappear once customer mix and years are accounted for.
- **H4:** the shop mostly *overestimates* hours, so a "costs that run over" hypothesis wasn't supported. I framed H4 the other way: estimates too high, losing quotes.

**Assumptions behind some sizes:**
- H1 measures excess material against a 30% material share of revenue, which I picked as a baseline.
- H7 uses an 8% cost of capital.
- H2 prices hours at the median pay rate, without benefits.
- Recovery rates in H3, H4 and H8 are guesses.

Lost customers aren't a separate hypothesis: few stop ordering. The most in any year was 12, with about $130k a year of revenue among them (q85).

Nothing in the records was addressed to an AI.
